item.title: 29-year-old Navneet Pillay’s family left grieving after locomotive accident
item.description: A Labasa family is struggling to come to terms with the sudden loss of their 29-year-old son, Navneet Pillay who died in a locomotive accident in Vunika. Speaking to fijivillage News, 59-year-old father of deceased, Deo Nadan Pillay, says the family initially did not know what had happened to Navneet.
item.content:encoded:
A Labasa family is struggling to come to terms with the sudden loss of their 29-year-old son, Navneet Pillay who died in a locomotive accident in Vunika.

Speaking to fijivillage News, 59-year-old father of deceased, Deo Nadan Pillay, says the family initially did not know what had happened to Navneet.

He says police arrived at around 6am and showed him a photograph of the deceased on a mobile phone, asking him to identify him.

Pillay says he immediately recognised the man as his son.

He says the family later went to the area where the incident occurred and saw blood at the scene, although Navneet's body was no longer there.

Pillay says Navneet was single and was one of his three children.

He says Navneet had previously worked at Coca-Cola before later working in the industrial sector.

Pillay says he could not say much about what caused the incident,but confirms it happened along the same stretch of track.

He says the headlight of the locomotive was on and there was a large fire following the incident.

Pillay says the family is now left to come to terms with the loss.

item.title: Korotasere brothers sow seeds of success through farming
item.description: For brothers Lui Teraka and Taniela Saukatamani, farming is more than a job, it is a way of creating a better future for themselves and their family. The two young farmers from Korotasere Village in Cakaudrove , Vanua Levu, are using the skills and discipline they gained at Tutu Training School in Taveuni to grow their farming business.
item.content:encoded:
For brothers Lui Teraka and Taniela Saukatamani, farming is more than a job, it is a way of creating a better future for themselves and their family.

The two young farmers from Korotasere Village in Cakaudrove , Vanua Levu, are using the skills and discipline they gained at Tutu Training School in Taveuni to grow their farming business.

They say their time at Tutu Training School has taught them more than just agricultural skills as they learned the importance of hard work, commitment, planning and making the most of every opportunity.

Those lessons continue to guide them as they work on their farm back home in Korotasere.

During his recent visit to Vanua Levu, Minister for Agriculture and Waterways Tomasi Tunabuna met the brothers as they returned from another day working on their farm.

Their story reflects the efforts of young Fijians who are turning to agriculture as a business and a way to build a sustainable future.

For Teraka and Saukatamani, the early mornings, long hours and challenges that come with farming, are part of the commitment needed to succeed.

They believe that with knowledge, patience and dedication, the land can provide opportunities for them and future generations.

item.title: 20 CCTV cameras in Ba to boost public safety and combat crime
item.description: Public safety in Ba is expected to improve with the installation of 20 CCTV cameras at key locations as part of a $77,050 project aimed at assisting Police in combating crime. Acting Chairman of the Ba Riverside Carnival Committee Anil Amin says the cameras will cover areas including the Ba Market, bus stand, main town, Varadoli and other identified areas.
item.content:encoded:
Public safety in Ba is expected to improve with the installation of 20 CCTV cameras at key locations as part of a $77,050 project aimed at assisting Police in combating crime.

Acting Chairman of the Ba Riverside Carnival Committee Anil Amin says the cameras will cover areas including the Ba Market, bus stand, main town, Varadoli and other identified areas.

In an interview with fijivillage News, Amin says the project is a long-term investment for Ba, and they want to ensure that people do not live in fear of crime.

He says this will benefit the town for years to come.

He says they have been advised by Fintec that the installation of the cameras will take about six weeks.

This follows the signing of an agreement with Fintec Solutions PTE Limited.

Amin says the CCTV network will be monitored from the Ba Police Station.

He says CCTV footage can also assist the Ba Town Council in taking action against people caught littering.

Am in says the project had been in the pipeline for about three years and was initially proposed to assist Police in combating crime in identified red-zone areas.

Insert: Amin on similar projects in future 18th Aug

He says he is pleased to see the project finally eventuate after first considering the idea three years ago, adding that the committee members have supported the initiative.

item.title: Ratu Peceli Rokoralovo found guilty of murdering Dr Leli Darling
item.description: Ratu Peceli Rokoralovo has been found guilty of murdering Nadi based Doctor Isireli Biumaitotoya, who was also known as Leighley Leli Darling, with the sentencing on 4th September. Rokoralovo attacked Dr Biumaitotoya with a cane knife at the deceased's residence in Fatima Court, Martintar, Nadi between 31st August and 1st September last year .
item.content:encoded:
Ratu Peceli Rokoralovo has been found guilty of murdering Nadi based Doctor Isireli Biumaitotoya, who was also known as Leighley Leli Darling, with the sentencing on 4th September.

Rokoralovo attacked Dr Biumaitotoya with a cane knife at the deceased's residence in Fatima Court, Martintar, Nadi between 31st August and 1st September last year .

During the trial, it was heard that Rokoralovo and Dr Biumaitotoya were involved in a complex personal relationship marked by financial dependence, jealousy, alcohol abuse and escalating conflict, culminating in a fatal attack at the deceased's home.

The prosecution said following an argument, Rokoralovo repeatedly attacked Dr Biumaitotoya with a cane knife, causing fatal injuries, before leaving the scene in the deceased's vehicle.

item.content:encoded:
The U.S citizen, Edward Zimbardi accused of running an alleged Ponzi scheme worth more than US$165 million, who was deported from Fiji to the United States to face federal charges, was living in a luxury island home here, and the question now arises on whether he had established local connections here.

The U.SÂ Embassy in Fiji confirm Zimbardi was deported on Friday following cooperation between Fijiâ€™s Ministry of Immigration, the Fiji Police Force and U.S. authorities.

FBI Supervisory Special Agent Aaron Sears who had come to Fiji says Zimbardi thought he could run off to a far-off Pacific island to avoid the FBI and live off the money he allegedly stole from his investors.

S ears says Zimbardi's life of luxury has come to an end and he now sits in a jail cell in the United States awaiting his day in court.

He adds what the FBI agents found in Fiji were upset leaders who did not want him in their country after they had found out what he is accused of doing back in the United States.

Several of the victims that the FBI had spoken to in this investigation had told them that Zimbardi told them that he had lost his money in the collapse of the program just like they did.

Special Agent Sears said vinaka to the Fijian Ministry of Immigration for the invaluable help that they provided in this investigation.

It was said that in an effort to avoid the reach of law enforcement, Zimbardi travelled internationally for years.

Last June, before criminal charges had been filed, the FBI encountered Zimbardi at the Atlanta-Hartsfield-Jackson Airport.Â

He told the agents that he had plans to fly to Fiji for a month, and Zimbardi took that trip but almost immediately after he arrived, he cancelled his return ticket to the United States.

U.SÂ Attorney for the Northern District of Georgia, Theodore S. Hertzberg says the FBI agents travelled to Fiji and in an undercover capacity escorted Zimbardi back to the United States and immediately arrested him upon touching down at LAX in California.

Zimbardi faces federal charges of wire fraud and money laundering in connection with the alleged scheme, which reportedly victimised thousands of people.

Hertzberg says Zimbardi allegedly tricked thousands of people into investing in his â€œCrypto Program” by promising huge returns.

He says Zimbardi allegedly used the money for risky currency trades, payments to early investors, a house and expensive vehicles instead.

Zimbardi faces wire fraud and money laundering charges.

fijivillage News has sent further questions to the U.S authorities. We are awaiting their response.
